beats.title: Dyed Flax Fibres Are Spun
beats.description: Hunter-gatherers in a Caucasus cave twisted and dyed wild flax fibres, the oldest known cloth-making thread.
beats.note: Sources give about 30,000 to 36,000 years ago; approximate

beats.title: Silk Weaving Begins in China
beats.description: Legend credits an empress with unravelling a silkworm cocoon, starting the making of the world's most prized fabric.

beats.title: The Silk Road Opens
beats.description: A Han envoy's journey west opened trade routes that carried Chinese silk across Asia to Rome.
beats.note: Zhang Qian's mission began 138 BCE; returned about 126 BCE; approximate

beats.title: Silkworms Smuggled to Byzantium
beats.description: Monks hid silkworm eggs in hollow canes and carried them to Constantinople, ending China's monopoly on silk.
beats.note: Some accounts say 563; 552 is the usual date

beats.title: Elizabeth I Gets Silk Stockings
beats.description: An English queen received a pair of knitted silk stockings and refused to wear cloth hose ever again.
beats.note: Sources give 1560, 1561 or 1562; 1561 is the most often cited

beats.title: Lee Invents the Knitting Machine
beats.description: An English clergyman built the stocking frame, the first machine to knit cloth, and was refused a patent by the queen.
beats.note: Traditional date; earliest documentary evidence is 1600

beats.title: Charles II Introduces the Waistcoat
beats.description: A king declared a new long vest and coat as court dress, the ancestor of the modern three-piece suit.

beats.title: Kay's Flying Shuttle
beats.description: A mechanical shuttle let a single weaver throw thread across wide looms far faster than by hand.

beats.title: Hargreaves' Spinning Jenny
beats.description: A multi-spindle spinning frame let one worker spin several threads at once, boosting yarn output.

beats.title: Arkwright's Water Frame
beats.description: A water-powered spinning machine produced strong cotton thread and led to the first cotton mills.

beats.title: Whitney Patents the Cotton Gin
beats.description: A machine to strip seeds from raw cotton made the fibre cheap to prepare and fed the textile boom.

beats.title: Jacquard's Programmable Loom
beats.description: A loom controlled by punched cards wove intricate patterns automatically, an ancestor of computer programming.

beats.title: Hermes Opens as a Harness Workshop
beats.description: A Paris saddler opened a shop that would grow into one of the most prestigious luxury fashion houses.

beats.title: Victoria's White Wedding Gown
beats.description: A young British queen chose white satin for her wedding, starting the fashion for white bridal dresses.

beats.title: Howe Patents the Sewing Machine
beats.description: An American inventor won a patent for a lockstitch machine that sewed with thread above and below the cloth.

beats.title: Bloomers Scandalise Fashion
beats.description: Women's trousers gathered at the ankle, worn under a short skirt, were promoted by reformers and mocked in print.

beats.title: Perkin Discovers Mauve Dye
beats.description: A teenage chemist stumbled on the first synthetic dye while seeking a cure for malaria.

beats.title: Worth Opens a Paris Couture House
beats.description: An English tailor in Paris began designing seasonal collections and showing them on live models, founding haute couture.

beats.title: Levi's Patent Riveted Jeans
beats.description: A tailor and a dry-goods merchant patented copper rivets on work trousers, creating blue jeans.

beats.title: Burberry Invents Gabardine
beats.description: A draper developed a tightly woven, weatherproof cotton twill that became the basis of the trench coat.
beats.note: Most sources say 1879; a few say 1880

beats.title: Viscose Rayon Is Patented
beats.description: British chemists patented a way to turn wood pulp into a silky fibre, the first widely made artificial fabric.
beats.note: Patent of May 1892; Wikipedia's lead says 1894

beats.title: Judson Patents the Zipper
beats.description: An American inventor patented a clasp locker for shoes, the forerunner of the zip fastener on clothes.

beats.title: The Modern Bra Is Patented
beats.description: A New York socialite sewed two handkerchiefs and ribbon into a backless undergarment and won a patent for it.

beats.title: Converse All Star Canvas Sneaker
beats.description: A rubber-soled canvas high-top was launched for basketball and became a casual footwear staple.
beats.note: Launched 1917 as the Non-Skid; renamed All Star in 1919

beats.title: Gucci Opens in Florence
beats.description: A former hotel porter opened a leather goods shop that grew into an Italian luxury fashion house.

beats.title: Chanel's Little Black Dress
beats.description: A magazine printed a simple black dress by Coco Chanel, which was likened to a mass-produced classic.

beats.title: Lacoste Launches the Polo Shirt
beats.description: A tennis star put a crocodile on a breathable piqué cotton shirt and began selling it to the public.
beats.note: Sales began 1933; he first wore it in play 1926-27

beats.title: Carothers Creates Nylon
beats.description: A DuPont chemist produced the first fully synthetic fibre, later made into stockings and parachutes.

beats.title: The Bikini Debuts
beats.description: A French designer unveiled a tiny two-piece swimsuit and named it after a Pacific atoll.

beats.title: Dior's New Look
beats.description: A Paris designer's first collection brought cinched waists and full skirts and defined postwar elegance.

beats.title: Hepburn's Givenchy Black Dress
beats.description: A long black evening gown and pearls in a film about breakfast at a jeweller became an icon of style.

beats.title: Marilyn's Sheer Birthday Dress
beats.description: A skin-tight, crystal-covered gown was worn to sing for a president, then sold for millions decades later.

beats.title: Mary Quant's Miniskirt
beats.description: A London designer shortened hemlines high above the knee, and the style swept youth fashion worldwide.
beats.note: Quant popularised it in the mid-1960s; Courrèges also claimed 1964

beats.title: Von Furstenberg's Wrap Dress
beats.description: A jersey dress that tied at the waist became a symbol of women's independence in the workplace.

beats.title: Air Jordan Sneakers Launch
beats.description: A basketball star's signature shoe in black and red was banned by a league yet became a global streetwear icon.

beats.title: Princess Diana's Revenge Dress
beats.description: A royal wore a daring, off-the-shoulder black dress to a gala on the night a rival story broke.

beats.title: J.Lo's Jungle Green Versace Dress
beats.description: A plunging silk chiffon gown at a music awards show was so popular it inspired the creation of image search.

beats.title: Crocs Clogs Debut
beats.description: A foam clog launched at a boat show turned into a divisive, colourful footwear craze.

beats.title: Lady Gaga's Meat Dress
beats.description: A pop star arrived at a music awards ceremony wearing a dress made of raw beef, sparking global debate.

beats.title: Kate Middleton's Wedding Dress
beats.description: A lace gown by Sarah Burton for Alexander McQueen was watched by a global audience at a royal wedding.
